Title: Inappropriate to portray pardon power as 'above the law', says Azalina
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: It is inappropriate to portray the exercise of the constitutional power of pardon as an act of being "above the law", said Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
She said the power of pardon was not outside the law, as it is provided for under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution.
Azalina, who is also minister in the prime minister's department, said that in respect of offences committed in the Federal Territories, Article 42 provides for the Yang di-Pertuan Agong's power of pardon and establishes the constitutional framework for the Pardons Board.

Title: Haze: Kuching, Serian among eight areas in Sarawak recording unhealthy air quality
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sarawak continued to bear the brunt of the haze this morning, with eight air quality monitoring stations in the state recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as at 8am today.
According to the latest data from the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Kuching and Serian recorded the country's highest API readings at 168.
Other areas in Sarawak that recorded unhealthy API readings were Samarahan at 163, Sri Aman at 161, Sibu at 160, Sarikei at 152, Bintulu at 151 and Kapit at 126.
In Perak, Seri Manjung recorded an API reading of 164, while Tanjung Malim recorded 118.
Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur recorded an API reading of 156, while Cheras recorded 155.
In Selangor, Shah Alam recorded an API reading of 156, followed by Petaling Jaya at 151.
Nilai in Negri Sembilan recorded an API reading of 151.
In Johor, Larkin recorded an API reading of 123, while Tangkak recorded 105.
Tawau in Sabah recorded an API reading of 122, while Bukit Rambai in Melaka recorded 107.
Overall, 37 stations recorded moderate API readings, while 10 recorded good air quality.
Under the API classification used by APIMS, readings of zero to 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are categorised as hazardous.

Title: Saudi Arabia issues Riyadh air raid alert, explosions heard
Article:
RIYADH: Explosions were heard in Riyadh on Saturday, an AFP journalists reported, after an air raid alert was issued by Saudi Arabian authorities, regularly targeted in recent days by pro-Iranian Houthis in Yemen.
This is the first time the capital has been directly affected since a conflict in neighbouring Yemen intensified in July.
"The area is under a hostile aerial threat," a message received shortly before 3am (0000 GMT) by residents of the Saudi capital warned, urging them to stay indoors.
AFP journalists then heard two explosions, and the alert was lifted about half an hour later by Saudi Arabia's civil defence agency.
The Houthis, who already held most of Yemen's populated areas, launched a lightning offensive this month to take over the country's entire Red Sea coast, giving them control over the vital Bab al-Mandab strait.
The group has declared a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia, which had been used to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, itself closed by the Middle East war, for its oil exports.
Figures from maritime tracking firm Kpler showed that Saudi exports via the Bab al-Mandab strait had dropped since July, although five loaded ships had passed through in the last week.
The Houthis insist that navigation of the strait is open and free except for Saudi vessels.
The UN said Friday that the renewed fighting had displaced more than 112,000 people while nearly 3,000 others had fled across the sea to Djibouti, heaping further misery on an already struggling population.--AFP

Title: AirAsia 'not too big to fail': Strategist
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Any government assistance for AirAsia Group Bhd should focus on preserving air connectivity, while leaving the airline to resolve its financing needs through private markets, an aviation strategist said.
The strategist, who declined to be named, told Business Times that AirAsia's importance to Malaysia did not necessarily make it "too big to fail."
"AirAsia is not too big to fail because it would not instigate the collapse of the country's monetary or financial sector," he said.
Instead, he said AirAsia could be regarded as "too critical to collapse" because of its role in domestic and regional connectivity, low-cost travel, tourism and employment.
The aviation strategist said excess capacity and fare competition had affected airline profitability in Malaysia and that the country should have managed capacity growth.
"The aviation policy should be based on managed capacity growth rather than a free-for-all environment. Then everybody can succeed," he said.
He added that Malaysia needs both full-service and low-cost airline products.
"A dual-carrier structure is necessary. Malaysia can achieve maximum economic output by maintaining a balanced, multi-tiered aviation market."
"The role of the government is to ensure regulatory stability and infrastructure support, allowing market-led restructuring to restore private balance sheets while safeguarding public funds," he said.
His comments come as AirAsia seeks up to US$1 billion from international debt markets and RM700 million in local credit facilities.
On Sept 2, AirAsia said in a statement that the fundraising is primarily intended for debt restructuring and refinancing as well as balance-sheet consolidation, rather than purely to fund operational shortfalls.
The group said it had raised about US$300 million in March to extend debt tenures and reduce principal obligations.
AirAsia Group reported RM5.1 billion in revenue and a net loss of RM830.5 million for the second quarter ended June 30, 2026.
For the first six months of 2026, revenue stood at RM11.04 billion while net loss was RM959.2 million.
AirAsia said its second quarter performance was affected by sharply higher fuel costs and RM331 million in foreign exchange losses.
Facilitate But Don't Bail Out
The strategist said the key policy question was not whether AirAsia is important to Malaysia but what form any government support, if considered, should take.
He said focus should be on protecting Malaysia's connectivity needs.
"My core stance would be to facilitate but don't bail out," he said, adding that the facilitation could include measures involving airports and maintaining regional connectivity.
The strategist said AirAsia's financing requirements should be addressed through private-market refinancing.
"It must be addressed through private-market refinancing. The government's role is not to provide a guarantee.
"Its role is to ensure regulatory stability and not absorb commercial risks," he said, adding that if any public sector assistance is being considered, its scope must be made clear.
Uncertainty Over Government Involvement
Endau Analytics aviation analyst Shukor Yusof said greater clarity over the government's role is needed amid reports surrounding AirAsia's fundraising.
"What I am more interested in is whether it is true that MoF is providing this guarantee or undertaking to help AirAsia obtain or raise money," he said.
Reuters reported on Sept 3, citing sources familiar with the matter, that the Finance Ministry has engaged Alton Aviation Consultancy (Alton) to assess AirAsia's funding requirements.
Reuters then reported on Sept 16 that discussions had included the possibility of some form of government endorsement to support external fundraising, although the nature of any potential assistance remained unclear.
Reuters also reported, citing sources, that the government has held discussions with Malaysia Airlines Bhd, a unit of Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG), and Batik Air Malaysia over their ability to absorb some of AirAsia's domestic capacity if required.
Shukor said continued speculation on AirAsia's situation and the government's role is also affecting the airline and its employees.
"I also think it's unfair to the airline itself if this speculation continues because it clearly affects the morale of the people who work there when they read all these negative things happening to their employer."
"We have to be fair to the airline, its employees, and also to its creditors and lenders," he said.
However, the aviation strategist said if AirAsia were to reduce its operations, other airlines could gradually add capacity to replace the gap.
He said the market could take between one and two years to normalise with additional capacity potentially coming from Malaysia Airlines, Batik Air and perhaps AirBorneo as their fleets expand.
But he said replacing AirAsia's capacity would not necessarily mean replacing its low fares as other airlines operate with different cost structures.
"(For example), Malaysia Airlines could come up and fill the capacity but don't expect them to drive capacity at low cost price," he said.
AirAsia's Reach Goes Beyond flying
Shukor said AirAsia has contributed to Malaysia through tourism, hospitality and employment.
"I think people who understand the business acknowledge AirAsia's importance to Malaysia's economy in terms of hospitality, tourism, job creation and all that," he said.
AirAsia Group, formerly AirAsia X Bhd, completed the acquisition of AirAsia Bhd and AirAsia Aviation Group Ltd in January bringing AirAsia-branded airline operations in Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, the Philippines and Cambodia under one aviation platform.
Meanwhile, Capital A Bhd focuses on businesses including Asia Digital Engineering, Teleport, AirAsia MOVE, AirAsia Next and Santan.
Shukor said changes in AirAsia's operations could also affect aviation-related businesses.
He said for example ADE, the maintenance, repair and overhaul business is important to Malaysia's aviation industry.
"ADE is very, very important not just for Malaysia Inc. but for the entire industry within Southeast Asia.
"It is an engineering company that provides substantial support to many other carriers. That is a very valuable asset," he said.

Title: PMI sees Malaysia as strategic hub
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's advanced manufacturing capabilities, supplier network and talent pool are strengthening its position as a strategic hub for Philip Morris International (PMI), with the company saying the country has an important role to play in its wider Asian operations.
PMI East and Southeast Asia and Global Travel Retail president Vassilis Gkatzelis said Malaysia's significance extended beyond its domestic market, with the country supporting the company's global supply chain and exports to about 80 markets.
He said PMI viewed Malaysia as a strategic location for advanced manufacturing, talent and supply chain resilience, citing an estimated RM6 billion in export value of PMI devices from the country between 2023 and 2026.
"Malaysia has a strategic role as a hub of talent, a hub of advanced manufacturing, and definitely a hub to ensure supply chain resilience around the world," he told the New Straits Times in an interview.
Gkatzelis said the company's operations had also created an ecosystem involving local suppliers, with about 3,400 jobs and collaboration with 400 Malaysian companies over the four-year period.
"We have a full ecosystem, and we trust the Malaysian ecosystem, not only in terms of manufacturing capabilities, but also in terms of talents.
"We're very happy to see that Malaysia is one of the most, I would say, advanced economies with strong growth and strong potential."
He pointed to Malaysian professionals holding leadership positions within PMI globally, including at its regional headquarters in Hong Kong, as another indication of the depth of the country's talent pool.
"We have many Malaysians who are creating an impact in Malaysia and beyond," he said.
Gkatzelis said Malaysia's strategic location was another factor behind its importance to PMI's regional operations, noting that the company had recently opened an office in Johor.
He also highlighted what he described as a "predictable and innovation-friendly policy environment" as an important consideration for businesses looking at long-term investment.
"We're always collaborating with stakeholders to always make improvements," he said.
The comments come as PMI continues to reposition its global business, with Gkatzelis saying the company had been building new capabilities and reshaping its organisation to respond to changing consumer and societal needs.
He said such a transformation required more than investment in new businesses, but also changes in the way a company approached talent, capabilities and long-term planning.
"PMI today is not the same PMI from 10 years ago or when I joined the company 23 years ago," he said.
Gkatzelis said the company's culture was built around three elements — better together in terms of collaboration, care and being "game changers" — which he described as part of PMI's corporate DNA.
He said that the emphasis on Malaysia's manufacturing, supplier and talent ecosystem reflects the country's role in the company's broader regional strategy, rather than simply as a market for its products.
Gkatzelis said the company remained confident in Malaysia's potential, particularly as the country sought to strengthen its position as a destination for higher-value investment and advanced manufacturing.
For Malaysia, he said attracting more high-value investments would require the country to continue anticipating future needs and strengthening its position as an innovation hub.
"Malaysia as a hub for innovation is important, and together, as an ecosystem, we need to look at what is ahead and proactively anticipate what is coming," he said.
"This will attract investment, but also sustainable growth. We're very confident in the future."
Gkatzelis also identified regulation and enforcement as important components of a business environment, particularly in tackling illicit trade.
He said illicit trade was a complex problem that required cooperation between governments, industry and other stakeholders, as well as cross-border collaboration.
"It starts with regulations, which are, of course, decisions of the government. But as an industry, together with different stakeholders, we're always providing learnings from other markets," he said.
He said evidence-based regulation, appropriate taxation and stronger cross-border cooperation were needed to tackle illicit trade.
Gkatzelis said the issue could have wider economic consequences, including lost tax revenue and jobs, while also contributing to criminal activity.
He cited cases in other markets like Australia, where illicit trade had been associated with violence against retailers, describing such incidents as "shocking".
"It is a global problem because some of this problem is linked to criminal organisations that are operating across countries," he said.
In Malaysia, Gkatzelis said PMI works with the Finance Ministry, Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry, Customs Department and other government agencies as part of a multi-agency approach to the issue.
"But I think the government has been making concrete efforts. So I would like to thank the authorities who have been collaborating together to combat this issue. That is not only happening in Malaysia, but around the world.
"It's a collaborative, multi-agency effort that we work together. A complex problem, but with concrete actions taken, and we hope that we are going to see the progress continue," he said.
ENDS

Title: OpenAI's Sam Altman to brief UNSC  as AI safety concerns grow
Article:
WASHINGTON: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman will brief the United Nations Security Council next week during the annual gathering of world leaders for the UN General Assembly, the company said Friday.
The meeting is being organised by France, which currently holds the rotating presidency of the 15-member Security Council, and comes as major players in the industry have said a slowdown in AI development could be necessary out of safety concerns.
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres on Wednesday called for coordinated international action to address AI risks as fears rise about the dangers of the fast-evolving technology.
"National action is essential. But global coordination is also indispensable," Guterres told reporters.
Concerns about AI safety have escalated in recent weeks, with workers at major AI developers resigning over concerns about the dangers posed by the technology.
Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei published an essay soon after urging caution.
"We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models," he wrote.
Altman and tech titan Elon Musk lent their support to the idea, as did Google DeepMind's Demis Hassabis, who himself has called for a US-led global regulatory body for the technology.
President Donald Trump has dismissed warnings against AI risks as a "hoax" and pushed back against calls for tighter oversight.--AFP

Title: Nvidia, OpenAI CEOs among tech leaders set for Xi dinner at White House
Article:
WASHINGTON: Nvidia boss Jensen Huang and OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman are among tech leaders expected to attend a White House state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping next week, a US official said Friday.
"It'll be a very popular and hot-ticketed event," the official said on condition of anonymity, adding that Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, SpaceX and Tesla chief Elon Musk, Apple head Tim Cook and Google CEO Sundar Pichai will also attend.
Their presence comes as artificial intelligence is set to loom large in the talks between the two leaders, with the United States and China the two dominant powers in the AI race.
The AI debate in the US remains dominated by the idea that the country's leading developers – OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta – cannot afford to slow their pace of innovation, whatever the risks, for fear that China will pull ahead.
China, long seen as trailing the United States on cutting-edge AI, has been closing that gap fast.
Washington has long tried to slow China's progress with export controls on the advanced chips needed for cutting-edge AI, blocking access to top-end US semiconductors such as those made by Nvidia.
Despite their bitter rivalry, hope remains that the two superpowers can agree on something regarding the technology when the leaders meet in Washington.
But anything ambitious, such as agreeing to slow development or craft global safeguards, is likely out of reach.
The call for safeguards has been amplified by dire warnings from industry insiders about the threat the technology poses to humanity.
Jacob Coxon, a former AI researcher at Anthropic, set off the latest round of alarm by describing how those building the technology "earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade."
Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei published an essay soon after urging caution and a slowdown in development.
Altman and Musk lent their support to that idea, as did Google DeepMind's Demis Hassabis, who himself has called for a US-led global regulatory body for the technology.
US President Donald Trump this week dismissed fears over AI as a hoax and is urging American AI companies to keep advancing to stay ahead of China.
According to analysts, Chinese policymakers have been more focused on immediate risks, from deepfakes to child safety.
However, the country's spy agency chief warned this week that the technology could jeopardise national security.--AFP

Title: Trump extends push for US$100,000 H-1B visa fee by another year
Article:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump has extended an executive order that would impose a fee of US$100,000 for H-1B non-immigrant visas by another year, the White House said on Friday.
US employers seeking to hire skilled foreign workers can use the federal government's H-1B visa program for a fee, allowing tech and other professionals from abroad to work in the United States for a few years.
Trump, who has pursued an aggressive immigration crackdown, has criticized the program and wants to permanently raise the fee from between US$2,000 and US$5,000 to at least US$100,000, though the attempt has faced legal challenges.
A Boston-based appeals court is reviewing a June decision by a federal judge who deemed the higher fee imposed by the Trump administration illegal and blocked the government from collecting it. Another court is considering whether a judge properly rejected a challenge to the fee by the US Chamber of Commerce, the largest US business lobbying group.
Trump's initial order for a fee hike, first released in September 2025, was set to expire this month. It did not apply to visas granted to foreign citizens already in the United States on student visas, who make up a large share of new H-1B recipients, or to renewals of current visas.
Despite criticism that some companies use the visas to hire lower-paid foreign workers instead of Americans, business groups and companies say they help recruit highly skilled professionals and address a lack of qualified US workers in some industries.
The visas, established by Congress in 1990, are especially critical for tech companies seeking to recruit from India and China.
Changes to how potential visa holders are scrutinised and processed have impacted companies' hiring and expansion plans, with some top H-1B users, such as Google parent company Alphabet , moving to increase operations in India.--REUTERS

Title: PPP calls for respect for Najib house arrest decision
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The People's Progressive Party (PPP) urged all parties to respect the decision granting former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak conditional house arrest.
Its president, Datuk Dr Loga Bala Mohan, said the outcome should be accepted as it was made through the constitutional Pardons Board process.
"The People's Progressive Party calls on all parties to respect and accept the decision of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia," he said in a statement yesterday.
Najib was granted house arrest for the remainder of his sentence on condition that he pays the RM50 million fine imposed following his conviction in the SRC International case.
The Federal Territories Pardons Board said in a statement that Najib must comply with all conditions imposed for him to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028.
It said His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, consented to the
conditional pardon
.
Loga Bala also called on all parties not to politicise the matter for personal or political gain.
"Differences of opinion are part of a democratic society, but they should be expressed responsibly and with respect for the Federal Constitution and the institutions of the country," he said.
Loga Bala said the party also expressed its appreciation to the Yang di-Pertuan Agong for considering Najib's application.
"Malaysia must continue to uphold the rule of law, constitutional institutions and respect for the Federal Constitution," he added.

Title: Woman killed after being run over by trailer
Article:
ALOR STAR: A cafe worker was killed after she fell from her motorcycle and was run over by a trailer in an accident at a traffic light junction near a shopping mall on Jalan Lencong Barat here yesterday.
Nur Atikah Umairah Suhaimi, 21, from Kampung Alor Pulai, Mukim Kangkong, died at the scene from severe injuries in the 5.50pm incident.
Kota Setar district police chief Assistant Commissioner Syed Basri Syed Ali said police received a call from a member of the public about the road accident involving the two vehicles.
He said preliminary investigations showed that the trailer and motorcycle were travelling in the same direction, from Masjid Aman towards the shopping mall and Taman Desa Seraya.
"When they reached the traffic light junction, the traffic light turned green and both vehicles began turning right.
"Suddenly, the trailer, which was on the right, grazed and hit the victim's motorcycle.
"The impact caused the motorcyclist to fall before she was run over by the trailer," he said in a statement today.
He said a urine screening test found that the 40-year-old lorry driver from Langkawi was not under the influence of drugs.
"However, investigations also found that he had five summonses, of which only one, involving an expired Motor Vehicle Licence, remained unpaid, while the other four had been settled.
"Police are also looking for witnesses who saw the incident to assist in the investigation.
"The vehicles involved have been detained for further inspection and the case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987," he said.

Title: Drug and scam syndicates busted, goldsmith hit a second time
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Major drug and scam syndicates, a corruption probe involving fertiliser supplies and a massive immigration crackdown were among the cases that kept enforcement agencies busy nationwide over the past week.
The period between Sept 11 and Sept 18 saw authorities pursuing more suspects linked to a RM2.4 billion drug laboratory, while Malaysians were arrested in Indonesia over an alleged online scam operation.
Closer to home, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigation into the delayed distribution of fertiliser to padi farmers in Kedah led to the arrest of a supplier company's managing director.
Meanwhile, hundreds of foreigners were detained during a major multi-agency operation in the heart of Kuala Lumpur, while authorities also moved against syndicates involved in fraudulent immigration documents.
Here is a recap of some of the major crime cases over the past week.
RM2.4 BILLION DRUG LAB PROBE CONTINUES
Police continued pursuing several individuals believed to be linked to the massive
drug-processing laboratory
uncovered at Eco Business Park V in Johor.
Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said police were pursuing between four and five more people believed to be part of the syndicate.
Drugs and equipment valued at about RM2.4 billion were seized from the facility, which police believe had been operating for more than a year.
The mastermind was believed to be a man who was shot dead by police during an anti-drug operation in Seremban.
The investigation also uncovered links between the syndicate and other cases being investigated by police.
30 MALAYSIANS ARRESTED IN INDONESIA OVER SCAM SYNDICATE
Thirty Malaysians were arrested by Indonesian authorities for allegedly operating an
online scam syndicate
from a hotel in Pontianak, West Kalimantan.
The suspects were believed to have targeted Malaysians.
The arrests again highlighted the cross-border nature of online scam syndicates and the involvement of Malaysians in operations based overseas.
ROBBERS ESCAPE WITH ALMOST RM1 MILLION IN JEWELLERY HEIST
Four masked robbers, armed with hammers and sharp weapons robbed a
goldsmith shop
in Bakar Arang, Sungai Petani, escaping   with jewellery worth between RM700,000 and RM1 million.
Police said the shop, located inside a supermarket, was also robbed in 2024, with losses estimated at RM1 million.
Investigations revealed the suspects arrived on two motorcycles. Two of them entered the shop while the other two waited outside.
They smashed the display cases before scooping up the jewellery.
BAJA 3 SUPPLIER COMPANY MANAGING DIRECTOR ARRESTED
MACC's investigation into the delayed distribution of additional compound fertiliser, known as
Baja 3
, to padi farmers in Kedah escalated with the arrest of the managing director of a fertiliser supplier.
The man, in his 30s, was arrested after turning up to give his statement at the Kedah MACC office. He was remanded for four days to facilitate investigations under Section 18 of the MACC Act 2009.
The investigation centres on issues surrounding the supply and distribution of Baja 3 to padi farmers in Kedah.
472 FOREIGNERS DETAINED IN LEBUH PUDU
A massive multi-agency enforcement operation around Lebuh Pudu in Kuala Lumpur saw
472 foreigners detained
for suspected immigration offences.
The operation turned chaotic as some foreigners attempted to flee, while several were involved in scuffles with enforcement personnel.
Authorities also uncovered several premises suspected of selling and storing illegal medicines.
Some were believed to have been operating makeshift clinics and were equipped with devices used for health screenings.
FAKE e-PLKS SYNDICATE BUSTED
The Immigration Department crippled a syndicate allegedly involved in producing and supplying
fraudulent electronic Temporary Employment Visit Passes (e-PLKS)
to foreigners.
Eleven Bangladeshi nationals were detained in the operation.
The syndicate allegedly supplied foreigners with fraudulent documents said to be legitimate employment passes.
Immigration subsequently intensified investigations to trace others believed to be linked to the syndicate.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump bans CNN, MS NOW and Politico from White House over 'fake news'
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Friday he was banning CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, accusing them of spreading "fake news" about his administration.
The 80-year-old Republican – who has long had a fiery relationship with the media – warned that other outlets could face a similar fate but did not say which ones.
The move by Trump drew immediate accusations that it was unconstitutional and would be thrown out by the courts, while the impacted news outlets said they would not be cowed.
"I am proud to announce that, effective immediately, I am banning Fake News CNN, MSNOW...and Politico...from the White House as a result of their constant 'reporting' FAKE NEWS!" Trump said on his Truth Social platform.
Trump did not say what prompted the move but added that "media Outlets shouldn't be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they're covering the President of the United States."
Later in the Oval Office, Trump told reporters: "I think that somebody has a right to keep them away if they're going to write false stories all the time."
Asked if any particular stories had sparked the ban, he replied: "It's really just cumulative stories over the last two years."
"You get sick of it," he said. "They purposely write negative news, and they do that because they want to try and diminish the Republicans and a Republican administration."
US Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth, a former Fox News host who has brought in tight restrictions at the Pentagon, backed Trump's new ban and accused the outlets of having "endangered troops" with unspecified stories.
- 'ILLEGAL ASSAULT' -
Journalists for broadcasters CNN and MS NOW – which was until recently known as MSNBC – and Politico remained on White House premises following Trump's announcement.
Reporters for the two TV news channels could still be seen broadcasting from their stations on the White House driveway.
CNN said Trump's ban was an "illegal assault" on US press freedom, adding that its reporting was "fair and accurate" and was protected under the US Constitution.
Politico vowed Friday to "vigorously defend our First Amendment rights against any attempt to restrict them."
The White House Correspondents Association – the independent body representing journalists covering the presidency – said it "stands in defence" of the journalists "who are being singled out for doing their jobs."
Both of Trump's White House terms have seen him lash out repeatedly at media whose coverage displeases him.
He has filed multiple defamation suits against news outlets, attacked the press on Truth Social and verbally assaulted several reporters, notably women, including CNN anchor Kaitlan Collins.
- 'FLATLY UNCONSTITUTIONAL' -
But it is rare for US presidents to outright bar news outlets – although Trump banned CNN reporter Jim Acosta in his first term, a ban which a court subsequently overturned.
Last year, Trump barred The Associated Press from some events because of the news agency's decision to continue referring to the "Gulf of Mexico" – and not the "Gulf of America" as decreed by Trump.
It has also put stricter controls on journalists in Trump's second term, including taking control of which outlets can cover events as part of the "pool" admitted to tight spaces such as the Oval Office and Air Force One.
Trump's surprise announcement on Friday comes at a time when his approval ratings are at record lows and his Republican Party risks losing control of Congress in November's midterm elections.
The war in Iran and rising prices, particularly at the gas pump, are among the factors that have contributed to his sinking political fortunes.
Bruce Brown, president of the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, said a ban on the media outlets would be "flatly unconstitutional."
"The First Amendment is clear that once the White House invites in some journalists, it can't ban others because it doesn't like their reporting," Brown said. "This is textbook viewpoint discrimination and will be quickly struck down by the courts if challenged."  --AFP

Title: Trump refuses to rule out demolishing Kennedy Center
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump refused to say whether he would attempt to demolish the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, the iconic facility on Washington's Potomac River.
Speaking from the Oval Office, Trump repeated his belief that the centre should append his name to the building in exchange for his work to raise money to renovate the facility.
He falsely claimed the centre faced long-term financial strains that required dramatic action, although the facility posted profits in seven of the past nine years, according to its tax filings.
"I think the Trump administration should be recognised as having saved the Kennedy Center because nobody else remembers," Trump said.
The Kennedy Center board, which has said the facility requires a US$257 million renovation, earlier this week voted to close the facility for two years for the project. US District Judge Christopher Cooper subsequently ordered the Trump administration to explain whether the closure violates a court order limiting its ability to shut down.
Cooper also ordered the administration to provide 30 days' notice before taking steps to demolish the building.
"President Trump is holding the Kennedy Center hostage," said Norm Eisen and Nathaniel Zelinsky, attorneys representing US Representative Joyce Beatty, an Ohio Democrat and ex-officio member of the centre's board who is leading litigation against the administration over its plans for the facility.
Representatives for the centre did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Friday.
The board, chaired by Trump and controlled by his appointees, earlier this year attempted to rename the facility the "Trump-Kennedy Center" and went so far as to add the president's name to the building. After Cooper ruled that only Congress could rename the centre, the board installed a tarp over the front facade of the building that has remained there as the legal fight continues.
Trump told reporters on Friday that adding his name to the building would be a show of "bipartisanship," because Trump is a Republican and Kennedy, who was assassinated in 1963, was a Democrat.
He called Cooper "hostile," and described the centre — which features a concert hall, opera house, theater and 12 additional performance and meeting spaces — as a "dump."--REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Relief for two ex-prime ministers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Two former prime ministers heaved a sigh of relief this week when one was allowed to serve his jail sentence under home arrest while the other walked free from four money-laundering charges.
The week was capped by a major legal development involving Datuk Seri Najib Razak, who was granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International prison sentence under house arrest.
This came about after the Federal Territories Pardons Board granted Najib a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine imposed in the SRC International case.
Earlier, former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin was acquitted of four Jana Wibawa-related charges involving RM200 million. Muhyiddin, however, still faces three separate charges in relation to the Jana Wibawa programme.
Also in the dock this week was former minister in the Prime Minister's Department Datuk Seri Jamil Khir Baharom who was charged with transactions involving RM860.3 million in Lembaga Tabung Haji assets.
Below are some of the other major court cases this week.
Najib granted conditional pardon, to serve sentence under house arrest
The decision on Najib's case, however, drew mixed reactions and sparked renewed debate over the use of house arrest for convicted prisoners.
Several quarters also sought clarification on how the arrangement would be implemented and monitored, as the specific conditions attached to Najib's house arrest were not immediately disclosed.
Under the conditional pardon, Najib must comply with the conditions imposed on him, failing which the pardon will be revoked and he will be required to return to prison to serve the remainder of his sentence.
The announcement also drew intense media attention, with reporters gathering outside Kajang Prison and Najib's residence in Langgak Duta, shortly after the decision was made public.
Muhyiddin acquitted of four Jana Wibawa charges
Muhyiddin secured a major legal victory on Tuesday when the High Court acquitted him of four of seven charges linked to the Jana Wibawa programme.
The prosecution informed the court that it did not intend to proceed with one abuse of power charge and three money laundering charges involving RM200 million.
The High Court subsequently granted the Bersatu president a discharge amounting to an acquittal on the four charges.
Muhyiddin, however, still faces three abuse of power charges involving RM25.3 million allegedly received by Bersatu in connection with Jana Wibawa.
The prosecution subsequently closed its case after calling 29 witnesses.
Jamil Khir charged over RM860.3 million in Tabung Haji assets
Jamil Khir was charged at the Sessions Court on Monday with three counts involving RM860.3 million in Tabung Haji assets.
He pleaded not guilty to charges of dishonestly causing the pilgrimage fund to dispose of the assets.
The charges concern transactions involving funds channelled to Al-Rawda Investment for Real Estate Development and Projects Management Co Ltd.
The court fixed bail at RM300,000 in one surety and ordered Jamil Khir to surrender his passport pending disposal of the case.
The case has been fixed for mention on Nov 5.
Teen acquitted in Bandar Utama schoolmate's murder
The Shah Alam High Court acquitted a 15-year-old boy of murdering his 16-year-old schoolmate at a secondary school in Bandar Utama after finding that he was of unsound mind at the time of the killing.
The teenager had been charged with stabbing the victim multiple times at the school last year.
The court found that he was suffering from severe schizophrenia and ordered him to be detained at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta for a period to be approved by the Sultan of Selangor.
The decision sparked renewed public attention after the victim's mother, Wong Lee Ping, urged the public to support a petition calling on the Attorney-General's Chambers to appeal against the acquittal.
She said the family respected the court and legal process but hoped the case would receive further consideration through any appeal available under the law.
Rosmah's fresh evidence bid put on hold
Rosmah's attempt to introduce additional evidence in her appeal against her conviction in the RM1.25 billion Sarawak solar hybrid corruption case was put on hold this week.
The Court of Appeal allowed the prosecution's application to stay an earlier order permitting Rosmah to adduce the evidence pending an appeal to the Federal Court.
The evidence involves prosecution witness Rayyan Radzwill Abdullah, a former consultant for Jepak Holdings Sdn Bhd.
The stay means further evidence from Rayyan will not be recorded for the time being.
Girl mauled by dog awarded more than RM500,000
A Johor court awarded more than RM500,000 in damages to a 10-year-old girl who suffered serious injuries after she was mauled by a dog.
The girl suffered facial fractures, paralysis and permanent scarring following the attack.
The case stood out among this week's proceedings for the severity of the child's injuries and the amount of the damages awarded.
Judicial Commissioner Noradura Hamzah found the dog's owner, fisherman Lim Seer Hao, fully liable for the attack and dismissed his counterclaim against the girl and her parents.
The award comprised RM193,000 in general damages, RM300,000 for future medical expenses and RM24,643.81 in special damages. The court also awarded costs of RM120,000.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Najib's house arrest could revive 'Bossku' sentiment, analysts say [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak's house arrest arrangement could revive his political influence and inject fresh energy into sections of Umno's grassroots, analysts said.
The move could reignite the "Bossku" sentiment and strengthen Najib's role as a symbol and rallying point for traditional supporters, they said, while easing some pressure within Umno over his imprisonment.
But they cautioned that the political impact would not be uniform and could create fresh challenges for the unity government.
Universiti Teknologi Malaysia Faculty of Social Sciences and Humanities director Associate Professor Dr Mazlan Ali said the decision could have an immediate psychological effect on Umno members who regard Najib's imprisonment as a longstanding political grievance.
He said Najib retained sentimental value among sections of Umno's grassroots despite having spent years in prison and his return home could improve morale among his supporters.
"The decision gives relief to
Najib's supporters and sections of the Umno grassroots. It could revive the 'Bossku' sentiment and strengthen the feeling among supporters that the party leadership had fought for Najib," he told the
New Straits Times
.
He said this could allow Umno to move beyond the prolonged
focus on Najib's imprisonment and concentrate on strengthening its organisation and preparing for the next general election.
But he cautioned that any boost in morale among Najib's supporters should not be interpreted as an automatic increase in wider public support for Umno.
He said Najib's
association with the 1Malaysia Development Bhd scandal and questions surrounding governance and integrity would continue to influence how some voters viewed the development.
National Unity Advisory Council member and political analyst Professor Datuk Dr Awang Azman Awang Pawi said the decision could provide "moral and psychological relief" to Najib's core supporters and sections of the Umno grassroots.
He said Najib could regain greater influence as a political symbol and driver of grassroots sentiment, even while remaining subject to the requirements of the conditional pardon and unable to necessarily return to political activity as before.
"Najib has the potential to become more influential as a symbol and driver of grassroots sentiment.
"He could become an asset to Umno in strengthening the loyalty of traditional supporters, particularly Malay voters who view him as a leader who brought stability and provided assistance to the people."
He said the development could also increase pressure within Umno for the party to be more vocal in defending Najib and raising issues surrounding justice and his pardon.
But Umno must handle the issue carefully as it is still part of the unity government, he added.
"The party cannot be seen as turning the decision into a political victory that challenges the sensitivities of its partners in Pakatan Harapan."
Universiti Malaya Department of Political Science, Public Administration and Development Studies senior lecturer Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said the decision could ease tensions among Najib's strongest supporters while creating political risks for the unity government.
"This decision provides moral and psychological relief to Najib's staunch supporters and part of the Umno grassroots.
"In the immediate term, it could revive the 'Bossku' sentiment and increase internal pressure for Umno to be more vocal in raising issues of justice, pardon and defending its former president."
He said Umno must balance the renewed sentiment around Najib with its position in the unity government.
He said Najib could regain influence as a political symbol and mobiliser among traditional Umno supporters, particularly Malay voters who continue to associate him with stability and aid.
"Najib can become influential again as a symbol and driver of grassroots sentiment. Although he remains subject to the conditions of the pardon and is not necessarily free to engage in politics as usual, he can become an asset to Umno in strengthening the loyalty of traditional supporters."

Title: US-Greenland security deal to boost Nato, Europe: Danish PM
Article:
COPENHAGEN: An agreement due to be signed by Denmark and Greenland with the United States giving Washington control over the autonomous Danish territory's security is "good for Nato and Europe," Denmark's prime minister said Friday.
Mette Frederiksen said the deal "strengthens our common security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic area," adding that it was expected to be signed on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly next week.
Trump said Friday that he had struck an "infinite" deal with Denmark to give the United States control over Greenland's security and bar foreign adversaries from setting up bases there.
"I am pleased to announce that the United States of America has entered into an Agreement with The Kingdom of Denmark, and Greenland, that gives the United States permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland," Trump said on his Truth Social network.
"From now on, no US adversary can EVER have a base in Greenland, have a military presence in Greenland, or make sensitive investments in Greenland, without our express written approval."
"It is gratifying that we are about to enter into an agreement that ensures and strengthens the security of Greenland, the Kingdom of Denmark, the United States and the Western alliance," said Jens-Frederik Nielsen, the head of reenland's government.--aFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump unveils 'infinite' deal for permanent US security control over Greenland
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Friday that he had struck a deal with Denmark to give Washington "permanent control" over Greenland's security that would bar Russia and China from setting up bases in the Arctic territory.
Since returning to the White House in January 2025, Trump has repeatedly insisted that Washington needed to control Greenland for strategic reasons, alarming Nato ally Denmark and sparking fierce pushback from the alliance.
Denmark and Greenland – an autonomous territory controlled by Copenhagen – both hailed the deal and said they would sign it on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York next week.
"I am pleased to announce that the United States of America has entered into an Agreement with The Kingdom of Denmark, and Greenland, that gives the United States permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland," Trump said on his Truth Social network.
"From now on, no US adversary can EVER have a base in Greenland, have a military presence in Greenland, or make sensitive investments in Greenland, without our express written approval."
The 80-year-old said it was an "'Infinite Life' Agreement, there is no end!" and said Washington would immediately start building up a large military presence in the territory.
- 'GOOD AGREEMENT' -
Trump has repeatedly warned about Russia and China trying to establish a foothold in Greenland amid a strategic battle for supremacy in a warming Arctic, and the State Department left no doubt that they would not be allowed to do so.
"This agreement guarantees that China and Russia cannot have a base in Greenland, they cannot send troops to Greenland, and the necessary mechanisms are in place to prevent investment in sensitive sectors," a State Department official said.
At the Davos economic forum this past January, Trump reached a purported deal with Nato Secretary General Mark Rutte over the future of Greenland, the terms of which have remained vague.
Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen had said Monday that she was "optimistic" that ongoing discussions with the United States and Greenland since January could resolve the dispute.
On Friday, she said she was "pleased that there is a prospect of a good agreement for Greenland, the Kingdom of Denmark and the United States," adding that it was "good for Nato and Europe."
Greenland Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen said the deal with the United States "strengthens" the territory's security.
- NATO TENSIONS -
Trump gave no details about how the deal would work, and it was not clear if it was linked to or substantially different from the Rutte deal.
But several media outlets have reported that the United States wants to open three new military bases in southern Greenland, in addition to the Pituffik base it already has in the north of the territory.
A 1951 defence pact, updated in 2004, already allows Washington to ramp up troop deployments and military installations on the island provided it informs Denmark and Greenland in advance.
At the height of the crisis, Trump would not rule out using force to seize the territory of 57,000 inhabitants, sowing anxiety within the EU and Nato.
Since then, tensions have cooled somewhat, and in an apparent move to assuage Trump, Nato launched a new mission to bolster security in the Arctic.--aFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: US court puts brakes on third-country deportations
Article:
WASHINGTON: A US federal appeals court on Friday broadly upheld a lower court ruling restricting a Trump administration policy of deporting undocumented migrants to countries that are not their own.
The three-judge panel of the US Court of Appeals for the First Circuit said people facing "third-country" deportations must be given effective notice ahead of time about where they are being sent to allow them to raise concerns about potential persecution.
Congress has made it US policy not to deport people to countries where their lives would be in danger or they could be subject to torture.
"An individual's right to contest removal to a country based on a fear of persecution in that country means little if one does not receive prior notice of the intended removal destination and a meaningful opportunity to contest that destination," said Judge Seth Aframe, writing for the unanimous three-judge panel.
Department of Homeland Security (DHS) policy "would deny access to that protection to a substantial swath of noncitizens who are sent to third countries with no notice of their destination," the judge said.
The Trump administration is expected to appeal the case to the conservative-dominated Supreme Court.
Donald Trump campaigned for president promising to expel millions of undocumented migrants from the United States and has taken a number of actions aimed at speeding up deportations since returning to the White House.
The Trump administration has defended third-country deportations as necessary since the home nations of some of those who are targeted for removal sometimes refuse to accept them.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nobel Prizes to carry greater cash value this year
Article:
STOCKHOLM: Winners of the coveted Nobel Prizes will receive more prize money this year after the Nobel Foundation bumped up the award from 11 million Swedish kroner (US$1.12 million) to 12 million (US$1.22 million), reported German Press Agency (dpa).
Nobel Prize money is taxable in the United States and many other countries, but it can be made tax-free if the winner assigns the money directly to charity before receiving it.
Named after their founder, the Swedish inventor Alfred Nobel, the Nobel Prizes have been awarded annually since 1901 – with few exceptions – in the categories of medicine, physics, chemistry, literature and peace.
Sweden's central bank, the Reichsbank, has also established a prize in economic sciences honouring Alfred Nobel.
The laureates are announced in early October each year, with the awards presented on December 10 – the anniversary of Nobel's death – at ceremonies in Stockholm and Oslo.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Maldives president thanks Malaysia for considering US$100mil currency swap facility
Article:
HYDERABAD: Maldives President Mohamed Muizzu thanked Malaysia for its decision to consider extending a US$100 million currency swap facility and expressed optimism that bilateral ties would grow stronger following Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's recent state visit.
In a post on X on Friday, Muizzu also welcomed Malaysia's agreement in principle to begin negotiations on a Preferential Trade Agreement (PTA), describing both initiatives as important steps towards strengthening economic cooperation and creating new opportunities for businesses and people in both countries.
"It was an absolute honour to host you, dear Prime Minister @anwaribrahim, on your landmark State Visit to the Maldives.
"I am extremely grateful for your decision to consider extending a short-term currency swap facility of USD 100 million through our central banks," he said.
On Sept 15, Anwar told Malaysian media after concluding his official visit that Malaysia had agreed in principle to support the Maldives' application for a US$100 million financing facility, which he described as a form of soft loan to be implemented through the monetary authorities of both countries.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the terms and mechanism of the facility were still being worked out by Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and the Maldives Monetary Authority (MMA).
Meanwhile, Muizzu said Anwar's Sept 14-15 state visit to the Maldives "has opened a dynamic new chapter in the enduring bonds of friendship between the Maldives and Malaysia".
"Our fruitful official talks have laid a strong foundation for the future, reaffirming our shared commitment to expanding cooperation in key areas, including trade and investment, education and healthcare, tourism and sustainable development, Islamic affairs, and defence cooperation," he said.
Among other issues, Malaysia and the Maldives have agreed to grow their cooperation in multilateral forums such as the United Nations, the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) and the Commonwealth.
The Maldives is a key recipient of support under the Malaysian Technical Cooperation Programme (MTCP).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KJ: BN-PH relationship, Anwar-Zahid ties at lowest point
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former Umno Youth chief Khairy Jamaluddin says the relationship between Barisan Nasional and Pakatan Harapan, as well as between Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, is at its lowest point.
Khairy, better known as KJ, said the mood at the 2026 Umno General Assembly reflected growing sentiment among delegates that the party's cooperation with PH had effectively run its course.
"Basically, the message is that we are only staying in the government until the general election, whenever that is, and after that, when we enter the general election, then we will fight each other.
"That's basically the message from the Umno general assembly," he said in a recent episode of the Keluar Sekejap podcast.
Khairy said he believed the sentiment was shared by the overwhelming majority of delegates at the assembly, who agreed with the view that Umno was "done with this whole Unity Government."
He said the sentiment was so strong that some delegates wanted a general election to be held immediately.
Khairy said the direction emerging from the assembly also pointed towards the possibility of Umno cooperating with Perikatan Nasional, particularly Pas, based on a formula similar to the one adopted in Negri Sembilan.
However, he said several issues surrounding such cooperation remained unresolved.
These included the distribution of parliamentary and state seats, arrangements in states currently governed by Pas, including the so-called SG4 states, as well as BN-governed states such as Pahang.
"Many things have still not been decided, but what is clear is that we are done with PH, we are done with Anwar, and we are ready to contest with cooperation perhaps with PN, Pas and we are ready to take over the government," he said.
Khairy said seat allocation would be among the key issues to be addressed if Umno and Pas were to work together at the next general election.
He cited Melaka as an example, saying BN's "base position is 21 or nothing", leaving little room for Pas to be allocated seats there.
He said the eventual outcome would depend on how the respective parties resolved outstanding issues, particularly the terms of any potential cooperation between Umno and Pas.
Meanwhile, former Umno information chief and Keluar Sekejap co-host Shahril Sufian Hamdan said the political landscape could still change, particularly if Anwar had sufficient time to navigate the remaining period before the next general election.
Shahril said the emergence of Umno as a party perceived to be in a stronger position could itself represent a significant shift in the political landscape.
He likened the situation to a football match in which a team that had been trailing had equalised and then moved into the lead.
He said Umno's conduct would therefore need to reflect its changed position rather than continue behaving as though it were still trying to catch up.
Shahril also said developments involving former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, Zahid's political positioning and the future of Umno-Pas cooperation could all contribute to further changes in the political landscape.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia recovers 3 more bodies from sunken ship in Java Sea
Article:
JAKARTA: A joint search and rescue team on Friday recovered three more bodies from a ship that capsized and sank in the Java Sea, bringing the death toll to nine on the sixth day of the search, the Indonesian Navy said, reported Xinhua.
Indonesian Navy spokesperson First Admiral Tunggul said naval divers entered the sunken vessel and found the bodies of two men and a woman.
Divers also recovered 210 items from inside and around the wreckage, which will be handed over to Indonesia's National Transportation Safety Committee for investigation, said Galih Nurna Putra, commander of the Indonesian Navy base in Banjarmasin.
The Virgo Transport 8 was carrying 243 people from Surabaya in East Java province to Banjarmasin when it capsized in bad weather early Sunday.
According to the latest official data, 108 people have been rescued, nine have been confirmed dead and 126 remain missing.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Khairy clarifies 'PM-in-waiting' remark on Zahid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former Umno Youth chief Khairy Jamaluddin has clarified that his description of Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi as a 'prime minister-in-waiting' was not an endorsement of Zahid becoming prime minister.
Khairy said his remark was based on his assessment that Zahid had articulated a broader vision for Malaysia, rather than delivering a speech focused solely on party politics.
"I said that it was a speech of a prime minister-in-waiting. Of course, the superficial comments from critics were, 'Ah, this is just to flatter him'.
"No, no. That was not the point. The point I was making is that he has given thought to what he wants to do when he becomes prime minister," he said in a recent podcast.
Khairy said he had listened to numerous Umno presidential policy speeches dating back to the era of Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and was familiar with Zahid's speeches as Umno president.
He said Zahid's latest address stood out because it outlined what he viewed as a vision for the country.
"I think this is the first time that he has outlined a vision for the country. It was not just a political speech, it was a speech about the country, a vision for the country," he said.
Khairy pointed to Zahid's reference to the "Blue Malaysia Agenda" and eight strategic initiatives aimed at preparing Malaysia for its centenary of independence in 2057.
Among the areas outlined, he said, were science and technology, the future economy, rural socioeconomic transformation and racial inclusiveness, as well as proposals relating to government revenue, including the Goods and Services Tax (GST).
"This is not a speech of just a normal party president. This is a speech of somebody who is auditioning for the post of prime minister," he said.
Khairy said, however, that whether Zahid would eventually become prime minister was a matter for voters to decide.
"Whether he will become prime minister or not is for the voters to determine. But my point is, this was not an ordinary party president speech.
"It was a speech of somebody who has greater ambition, who is saying that, 'I'm ready, this is my vision, this is my vision when I become prime minister later'," he said.
Meanwhile, former Umno information chief Shahril Hamdan, who co-hosted the podcast, said he believed Khairy's wording also contained an element of ambiguity.
Shahril said Khairy's communication style allowed people to interpret the remark differently, including those who supported Zahid.
He said Khairy's underlying message was that Zahid was positioning himself as someone seeking the prime minister's post.
Khairy had previously said Zahid's policy speech at the party's general assembly showed that Umno and Barisan Nasional were ready to form the next government.
The former Umno Youth chief had described Zahid's policy speech as "the speech of a
prime minister-in-waiting
" after Zahid delivered his presidential policy speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly.
"This is the speech of a prime minister-in-waiting, and a speech of a government-in-waiting," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UN holds third informal poll for new chief
Article:
UNITED NATIONS: The UN's most powerful body, the Security Council, met Friday to again gauge the popularity of contenders to lead the organisation as world leaders prepare to gather for its annual signature event.
No frontrunner emerged from the first two rounds of informal straw polls, with eight candidates now vying to follow Secretary-General Antonio Guterres when his term concludes at the end of December.
Guyanese ex-foreign minister Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett narrowly led the second round of the secret process, while Costa Rica's Rebeca Grynspan came in second and Argentina's Rafael Grossi, the current head of the UN nuclear watchdog, was third.
Other candidates include Macky Sall of Senegal, Ecuador's Ivonne A-Baki, Chile's Michelle Bachelet, Ecuador's Maria Fernanda Espinosa and Uganda's Olara Otunnu.
There is speculation that a compromise candidate could be parachuted into the process at the behest of the powerful five veto-wielding Security Council members – Britain, China, France, Russia and the United States.
"If that happens in a way that's not transparent... then we have a problem," said one diplomat who asked not to be named due to the sensitivity of the matter.
Even if a candidate earns the required nine votes from the 15-member Security Council, they must also avoid a veto by any of the five major powers, which are deeply divided.
Once a candidate clears those bars, their name will go to the General Assembly of all UN members for confirmation.
Without singling out a favourite, a US State Department official said Thursday that candidates must get the UN "back to basics and publicly commit to the changes we require."
"Any new secretary-general must return the UN to its primary purpose of maintaining peace and security in the world, rather than the absurd, politicised, woke ideology that has undermined the institution's effectiveness," the official said.
'Muddled picture'
International Crisis Group's head of UN affairs Daniel Forti said "we'll be watching out for... whether any one or two candidates consolidate support from the council, or whether we sort of continue to be in a pretty muddled picture that gives more avenues for other potential contenders to jump into the race."
Each of the 15 Security Council members must anonymously assign each candidate one of three labels: "encourage," "discourage," or "no opinion."
But after an unspecified number of votes, the ballots of the Council's five permanent members will have a different colour, making it possible to identify potential vetoes, without knowing which country blackballed any given candidate.
Forti said it was thought there would be another straw poll at the end of the UN signature high-level week, though that is unconfirmed.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Norway's King Harald laid to rest in CO2-absorbing sarcophagus
Article:
OSLO: Norway's King Harald V has been entombed within a ship-shaped sarcophagus carved from a carbon dioxide-absorbing ancient rock, the palace revealed on Friday.
Next to no details of the late monarch's final resting place had previously come to light in the wake of his funeral in Oslo on Sept 9 and death aged 89 on Aug 28.
Installed in the royal mausoleum at the Akershus fortress, the sarcophagus is fashioned from olivine, a greenish rock dating back some 400 million years mined in western Norway, the palace said in a statement.
The coffin's shape nods both to ancient boat-burial traditions, such as those practised by the Vikings, and the late king's love of the sea, the palace added.
A two-person design, the sarcophagus also has space for Harald's widow, Queen Sonja.
"The greenish olivine stone can absorb and sequester carbon dioxide, a property that the designers chose as a symbol of King Harald and Queen Sonja's love of nature and their concern for future generations," the palace said.
In life, the late king was known to make light of what his coffin might look like.
"I hope it has good padding so that our stay will be comfortable. We're going to be staying there for a while, after all," Harald joked.
The 20-million-kroner (US$2.1 million) sarcophagus lies next to two others.
One, in white marble, holds the remains of the current ruling dynasty's first king, Harald's grandfather Haakon VII, and his wife Queen Maud. The other, in dark green bronze, houses Harald's parents, King Olav V and Crown Princess Martha.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KJ: Melaka polls may offer first glimpse of political impact from Najib pardon
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Melaka election could provide an early indication of how the political landscape responds to the conditional pardon granted to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, says Khairy Jamaluddin.
Speaking on the latest episode of the Keluar Sekejap podcast, Khairy, better known as KJ, said the election would be the first major electoral development where the political and public reaction to Najib's house arrest could be observed.
The former Umno youth chief described the Melaka poll as a potential "first key data point" following the latest development involving Najib.
"I think that will be the first key data point. Because when Melaka comes, all of this will already be priced in.
"The rakyat would have had time to digest Najib's release, what happened at the Umno General Assembly and the decision in Melaka," he said.
Khairy said the response in Melaka could provide an early indication of whether the development had changed the political equation for Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and other parties.
The Federal Territories Pardons Board on Sept 18
granted Najib

Title: Mural of rapper Macklemore painted in Gaza after Sheeran tour furore
Article:
GAZA/JERUSALEM: Artists in Gaza have painted a mural of Macklemore wrapped in a Palestinian flag on a huge slab of concrete in the ruins of Gaza City, after the US rapper was kicked off Ed Sheeran's upcoming tour for calling for a "Free Palestine".
The mural, on a slab that leans against ruined buildings surrounded by rubble, depicts the "Thrift Shop" rapper raising a fist in the air.
"Thank you for using your voice for Palestine," it reads.
"We wanted to send a message to thank rapper Macklemore in this simple way," said Anne Redwan, 26, who designed and painted the mural with fellow artist Qusai al-Helo.
"As an artist living under siege here in Gaza, we are waiting for support from anyone who can see (the) persecution we live under," she told Reuters. "We can paint murals bigger than this to express our feelings."
Macklemore, who has long supported Palestinian causes, was cut from British pop star Sheeran's musical lineup over remarks on stage criticising Israel's military assault in Gaza, which was launched after Hamas-led fighters attacked Israel in October 2023.
Sheeran said he was unable to keep Macklemore on the tour after stadium owners refused to let him appear. US billionaire Robert Kraft, owner of Gillette Stadium in Massachusetts where his New England Patriots football team plays, said he had barred Macklemore from appearing there for antisemitism, which the rapper denies.
Nearly a year after a ceasefire ended major fighting in Gaza, reconstruction has yet to begin. Most buildings have been destroyed and more than two million residents are confined to around a third of the enclave's territory, mostly in tents or crowded rooms in damaged buildings among the ruins.
A US-brokered plan to end the war has stalled, with negotiators failing to agree conditions for Hamas to disarm and Israel to withdraw its troops.
The furore over Sheeran's tour has led to a series of pledges from those involved to send money. Macklemore said on Wednesday he would donate his US$1 million in net earnings from the tour to six aid groups supporting Gaza.
Kraft, in turn, said Sheeran had told him he would donate US$2 million for aid in the region, and had asked him to match the pledge. Sheeran has not commented on any donations. Macklemore's donation drew a matching US$1 million pledge from Ms Rachel, a popular children's TV personality.
Aid agency officials said the boost in celebrity attention could help bring more support to Gaza, where nearly all residents rely on aid for food, water, medical care and shelter.
"But what's really most important is that people who have been so generous keep fighting over a sustained time," said Toby Fricker, a local official with UNICEF. "That's why we really call for sustained support, not one-off peaks, but sustained."
Hussein Murtaja, who runs a Gaza humanitarian group that provides mental health support to children, said Macklemore's solidarity matters more than the money he donated.
"When artists of this stature, with this many followers or fans, all come to know more about the cause, and support reaching a political solution, support achieving peace for the people of Gaza... That means a great deal to us."
